edit.description: a freed slot re-reads the queue and re-selects from it, skipping an attempted set rather than splicing a wave-start snapshot, and reads the stop flag beside the teardown signal
the mid-wave higher-priority pull, the mid-wave stop, and the never-re-picked pin, beside the wave's refill cases

summary: A freed slot refills from the wave-start snapshot and reads only the teardown signal, so an entry filed mid-wave waits out the whole queue and a flag written mid-run stops nothing

per.section: Fanout and worktrees — provisioning, isolation, teardown

acceptance: a freed slot reads the queue as it stands and re-selects in priority order, skipping every entry this wave has attempted, and reads the stop flag off disk through the reader the supervisor already spends, so an entry filed mid-wave at a higher priority is pulled ahead of lower-ranked work the wave started with, a flag written mid-wave pulls nothing more while every in-flight entry finishes and merges, and the wave ends when nothing it has not attempted is pickable
tests: a wave pulls an entry filed mid-wave at a higher priority before a lower-ranked one it started with
a wave pulls nothing more once the stop flag is written while a slot's agent runs
pins: a wave never pulls an entry it has already attempted
notes: Rulings 68eba4eb and e74af849, folded as both records asked. `fillSlots` (`src/waveTick.ts:386`) picks from `remaining` (`:249`), the wave-start snapshot, and guards on `leg.attemptCtx.stopSignal` alone (`:390`). `readPendingForDecision` (`:79`) with `leg.selection` (`:116`) is the re-read; `existsLoud(stopFlagPath(flumeDir))` (`src/loopSupervisor.ts:908`) is the flag reader to share, sync and already loud. `fillSlots` must stay sync: await the re-read in the settling slot's continuation.
